name: Pistol Squat
tierNote: Safety tier A from content.md appendix B (high skill). census.json difficulty tier 1.
parentNote: Full card. content.md appendix A lists pistol_squat as a stand-alone parent; census puts it in the single-leg family. Neither LB4A template parent fits (back squat: on-body hand; box jump: airborne).

claims.text: Stand tall, arms reaching forward for balance, and shift onto one leg while lifting the other forward.

quotes.text: Start standing tall. Extend your arms out in front of you to support your balance and shift your weight onto one leg while lifting the other up off the floor towards your arms.
quotes.where: How to Do Pistol Squats, step 1

claims.text: Brace, then send the hips back as the knee bends into a single-leg squat, keeping the free leg off the ground.

quotes.text: Engage your core and squeeze your glutes before sending your hips back as you bend your knee and lower down into a single-leg squat. Keep that non-working leg lifted off the ground.

claims.text: Go as low as mobility allows, ideally hamstring on calf, with the standing foot flat.

quotes.text: Go as low as mobility allows — ideally into a position where your hamstring and calf are touching — keeping your planted foot flat on the ground and your other leg lifted.

claims.text: Breathe out and press through the standing foot to stand.

quotes.text: Now to come back up to standing, exhale as you press through your rooted foot to push back up.

claims.text: The free leg hovers in front with a straight knee.

quotes.text: Your other leg should hover in front of you with a straight knee.

claims.text: The pistol squat is advanced; beginners should master basic squats and lunges first, and move on to assisted pistols once air squats and one-leg balance are comfortable, or practise to a box or bench behind you.

quotes.text: No, pistol squats are an advanced exercise and should not be attempted by beginners.
If you are a beginner, you should focus on mastering basic bodyweight exercises such as squats, lunges, and push-ups before attempting more advanced exercises such as pistol squats.
If you're comfortable and confident tackling air squats, balancing on one leg, and have given your ankles some dedicated mobility work, you're ready to move on to assisted pistol squats.
quotes.where: How to Work Up to Your First Pistol Squat

quotes.text: practice your pistol squat with a box or bench behind you.

claims.text: Load progression: single-leg balance and air squats first, then assisted pistols (holding a support to take weight off), squats to a box behind you lowered over time, and lowering-only reps.

quotes.text: Take some of the load off that working leg by utilizing a chair, pole, resistance bands, a doorframe
If you're comfortable and confident tackling air squats, balancing on one leg, and have given your ankles some dedicated mobility work, you're ready to move on to assisted pistol squats.
quotes.where: How to Work Up to Your First Pistol Squat

quotes.text: practice your pistol squat with a box or bench behind you.
Complete your single leg squat until you're seated on that box or bench, then press back to standing.
swapping the bench or box out for a lower target
Using proper pistol squat form, lower down on one leg, then stand up using both legs.

claims.text: Common mistakes: bouncing at the bottom, the knee caving in, and the heel of the standing foot lifting.

quotes.text: Bouncing at the bottom: This movement should be slow and controlled, without any bounce at the bottom of the squat.
Knee Valgus (aka your knee collapsing inwards)
Heel lift: As you lower down in that squat, your planted heel may try and creep up on you.

claims.text: The deep single-leg position puts real demand on the knee; with knee pain, back off, check form or use an easier version.

quotes.text: Because the pistol squat is a deep, single-leg movement, there’s a good amount of stress and demand placed on your knees. If you feel pain in the ole’ bendy bits, dial back your efforts with this move, check your form, or try some regressions or alternatives

claims.text: Quads are the main movers; glutes steady the hips and help stand; adductors of the working leg steady the knee.

quotes.text: Quadriceps: These are the main event, the major movers here, controlling your descent and powering you back to standing.
Glutes: The glutes stabilize your hips and support your quads as you fire back up out of that deep pistol squat.
On the working leg, your adductors

claims.text: Adding weight raises the strength challenge and can act as a counterbalance that helps keep you steady.

quotes.text: Adding weight increases the strength challenge and can actually act as a counterbalance, helping to keep you steady.

claims.text: NHS knee pain: get advice from 111 if the knee is very painful, or locks, gives way or painfully clicks.

quotes.text: your knee is very painful
your knee locks, gives way or painfully clicks – painless clicking is normal

plate.viewWhy: The free leg held forward (p5), depth (p3) and heel lift (p8) read from the side; a front view would hide the free leg behind the standing leg.
plate.start: Standing tall on one leg, arms forward, free leg lifted forward (p1).
plate.end: Bottom: hips back, standing knee fully bent, hamstring near the calf (p2, p3), standing foot flat (p3), free leg straight and hovering forward (p5), arms forward (p1).

checkpoints.label: Free leg straight
checkpoints.what: The free leg hovers in front, knee straight.

mistake.what: The heel of the standing foot lifts at the bottom.
mistake.why: Listed as a common mistake (p8); the technique asks for the planted foot flat (p3).
mistake.rankNote: REP lists three mistakes without ranking. Knee valgus is front-view; bouncing is a motion, not a pose. Heel lift is the one that can be drawn from the side.

tempo.text: Slow and controlled, no bounce at the bottom; no source gives seconds.

grip.note: Hand archetype none. Arms reach forward for balance (p1).

setup.step: Build up first: single-leg balance, air squats, then assisted or box pistols.
Shift onto one leg and lift the other forward, knee straight.
Brace, then send the hips back and bend the knee.

posture.point: Free leg straight, off the floor.
Hips go back as the knee bends.

handlingMistakes.mistake: Trying the full pistol before the basics.
handlingMistakes.fix: Master air squats and single-leg balance first, then use support or a box.
Lower slowly and stand without a bounce; use a box if you cannot.
Back off, check your form, or use an easier version.

rows.means: The deep single-leg bend is too much for now.
rows.fix: Use a box or support, or an easier version.

rows.where: Very painful knee, or the knee locks or gives way

risks.risk: High knee demand in the deep single-leg bend.
Advanced skill: attempting it before the basics.

zooms.right: Standing foot flat at the bottom.
zooms.wrong: Heel lifted, weight on the toes.

zooms.right: Single-leg squat down to a box behind you.
zooms.wrong: Dropping onto the box instead of squatting down to it under control.
zooms.wrongNote: The wrong drawing is the inverse of p7 (squat down until seated on the box); no source describes it directly.

libraryDiff.why: Library: quads primary, glutes and abductors secondary. REP names quads as main movers and glutes and the working-leg adductors as helpers (p10), so adductors are proposed as an addition. Abductors are not named by any source read (REP and Physitrack read in full), so removal is proposed for the supervisor to decide; no source supports keeping them. Coach source only, no EMG.

loadProgression.text: Single-leg balance and air squats, then assisted pistols, box pistols with the box lowered over time, and lowering-only reps.

wayOut.text: A box behind you to sit onto, or a support to hold, while learning.
